page.title: How to Choose a Community Engagement Strategy Consultant
page.description: A practical guide to evaluating consultants who design community purpose, member value and governance before any platform decision.
page.h1: How do you choose the right community engagement strategy partner?
page.definition: A community engagement strategy consultant is an advisor who defines community purpose, audience segments, member value propositions and governance models before a platform is selected, ensuring the program serves business goals rather than software features.
page.quick_answer: Hire a consultant who starts with purpose and member value, shows a governance framework, and treats platform choice as a late-step decision. Ask for a written assessment, prioritised use cases and a 90-day roadmap before signing.

sections.h2: What should the consultant deliver in the first engagement?

blocks.p: The consultant output is an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap.

ul: Current-state audit of audience, content and moderation gaps
Member journey map with value moments identified
Governance model covering roles, escalation paths and risk thresholds
Prioritised use cases ranked by business impact and effort
Platform shortlist tied to use cases, not vendor relationships
Ninety-day roadmap with owners, metrics and review dates

sections.h2: How do you evaluate strategic approach versus platform bias?

blocks.p: A strategy-first partner proves they separate purpose from technology by showing work where platform choice came last.

ul: Ask for a case study where the recommended platform changed after the use-case workshop
Require a written statement that platform selection occurs after governance and value design
Check that the consultant has no reseller agreement with any community platform
Confirm they have migrated communities between at least two different platforms
Verify they measure success by member retention and contribution, not login counts

sections.h2: What governance artefacts must exist before launch?

blocks.p: Governance is the operating system for the community; without it the platform is an empty room.

ol: Community charter stating purpose, values and success metrics
Moderation policy with escalation matrix and response-time SLAs
Member onboarding sequence with first-value milestone defined
Content and programming calendar owned by a named editor
Data privacy and consent workflow aligned to regulations
Monthly health dashboard template with leading indicators

sections.h2: How do you structure the first 90 days to prove value?

blocks.p: A first plan runs 90 days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course.

ul: Week one to two: stakeholder interviews, data audit, charter draft
Week three to four: use-case prioritisation, platform shortlist, governance sign-off
Week five to six: onboarding flow build, moderation team trained, pilot group invited
Week seven to eight: pilot feedback, metric baseline, programming calendar live
Week nine to ten: health dashboard review, roadmap adjustment, stakeholder readout
Week eleven to twelve: decision point on scale, scope or sunset

faq.q: What platforms do community strategy consultants typically work across?
faq.a: Common platforms include Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups. A strategy-first consultant evaluates these against your governance needs rather than defaulting to one.

faq.q: How much does a community strategy engagement usually cost?
faq.a: Consultants charge day rates or fixed project fees; agencies quote a fixed build fee plus a monthly retainer. West Peek Productions quotes Community as a Service by scope covering coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming.

faq.q: What is the difference between community strategy and community management?
faq.a: Strategy defines purpose, audience, value proposition, governance and platform fit. Management executes moderation, onboarding, programming, support and reporting. Keep strategy and brand voice in-house; outsource operational roles.

faq.q: When should you involve legal and security in the process?
faq.a: Bring legal and security into the governance workstream before the platform shortlist is finalised. They must approve data handling, consent flows, moderation liability and export controls before any member data enters a platform.

faq.q: How do you measure ROI on a community engagement investment?
faq.a: Track owned audience growth such as email subscribers and community members, not rented followers. Measure activation rate, contribution depth, retention cohorts and pipeline influence. Events and webinars convert attention into owned audience; West Peek Productions produces them from twenty-five hundred dollars per moderated webinar.
